description_full: Fortive Corporation designs, develops, manufactures, and markets products, software, and services in the United States, China, and internationally. It operates through Intelligent Operating Solutions and Advanced Healthcare Solutions segments. The Intelligent Operating Solutions segment provides advanced instrumentation, software, and services, including maintenance, repair, measurement and condition monitoring, facility and asset lifecycle software applications, and connected worker safety and compliance solutions for manufacturing, process industries, healthcare, utilities and power, communications and electronics, and other industries. This segment markets its products and services under the ACCRUENT, FLUKE, GORDIAN, INDUSTRIAL SCIENTIFIC, INTELEX, and SERVICECHANNEL brand names. The Advanced Healthcare Solutions segment provides critical workflow solutions comprising instrument sterilization, instrument tracking, biomedical test tools, radiation detection and safety monitoring, and end-to-end clinical productivity software and solutions under the ASP, CENSIS, FLUKE BIOMEDICAL, LANDAUER, and PROVATION brand names. Fortive Corporation was incorporated in 2015 and is headquartered in Everett, Washington.

financial_summary: Fortive Corporation is a large-cap technology business with a $20.2B market cap on $4.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -11% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 7% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 57% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $978M in free cash flow — roughly 24 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.87× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.4× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 6.0×.

Management returns a meaningful 8.4% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Its 17% operating margin runs 11pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.74x).
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-9.2% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 12% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 1% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 28% and a beta of 0.99, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.44 vs 5y 0.98), so read it loosely.
Liquidity is deep, with about $123.6M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 47% in the 2020 crash and 27% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 27% below its DCF fair value of $93.26, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 43%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $63.53 to $139 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/FCF 20.7 vs 26.1 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 100% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 4.8% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 3.1% (vs the 8% bar).
The 14 covering analysts target $67.50 on average, 1% below the price.
prof: ROIC of 7% falls short of the cost of capital of 8.8%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.51).
It runs a 57% gross margin and converts 24% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.87x.
ROE of 9% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.8x equity multiplier).
It spends 6.2% of revenue on R&D and 2.8% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 2.4x net debt to EBITDA ($375.5M of cash against $3.2B of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 6.0x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 3.4, in the safe zone).
The current ratio of 0.71 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
Goodwill makes up 62% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -10.6% over 3 years and -2.1% over 5 years, so the decline is deepening, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 18%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded -6.4% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.02, a backlog worth 20% of annual revenue and deferred revenue down 24%.
Capex runs only 0.2x depreciation (2.5% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 19, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.5%), and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (5 sales, net $8.3M sold).
It returns 8.4% a year to shareholders (8.0% in buybacks and 0.4% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 3.7% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 10,000 employees, each generates about $416K of revenue, in line with the Technology median, and revenue has fallen 4.4% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $98K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.5M (6x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (9/10, lower is better).
